content.thinking:
The flag actually flipped off→on at 23:28 according to the logs, causing the ZeroDivisionError, even though the change record timestamps it at 23:33:01. Then Argus's remediation attempts get confusing—it switched the flag off at 23:33:24 and back on at 23:36:27, so I need to untangle which action was the "already tried" fix.

Since there were no deployments in the window and memory stayed flat, the feature flag remains the strongest explanation—I'll set it as primary with high confidence, and offer a low-confidence secondary hypothesis that a latent defect in spend_summary.py was simply exposed by the flag rather than newly introduced.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on, and the newly enabled monthly-spend code path throws ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35 on account page renders. The error rate jumped from ~1% to ~30%+ in the exact minute the flag evaluations flipped from all-off to mostly-on (23:28), with no deploy or config change anywhere in the lookback. Argus's attempted disable did not restore service because the flag evaluations kept reporting 'on' afterwards (the off was re-flipped/never took effect), not because the flag is the wrong cause.
